chunks: From him, from 'Imran ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Qummi, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: 'A man sets out for hunting for a journey of a day or two days; does he shorten the prayer or complete it?' He said: 'If he sets out for his sustenance and the sustenance of his family, he should break the fast and shorten the prayer. And if he sets out for seeking luxury/excess, then no, and no honor (for him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayers and fasting for a hunter traveling for a day or two?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the intent behind the journey determines the legal status of the traveler, distinguishing between necessity (sustenance) and luxury (excess). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the purpose of travel dictates whether one is considered a traveler eligible for concessions (qasr and iftar) or a resident bound by full obligations. It underscores the importance of intention (niyyah) in determining the applicability of travel rulings in daily life.
